title: A small dictionary before you sink
lede: Japanese terms and fan terms used across the site. Any dotted-underlined word on any page can be hovered or focused to open its definition.
intro: Shikaku is a dense short story: almost every term in it carries two meanings at once. This glossary exists so readers new to Japanese can still catch the wordplay behind the title without opening a dictionary in another tab.
Definitions are written in our own words and kept short. When a term belongs to fan culture rather than the story itself, we say so clearly.

terms.short: An assassin; a killer sent to eliminate a specific target.
terms.long: A somewhat classical word for a hired killer. 刺 means to stab, 客 means guest or person. It is both the protagonist's profession and her name.

terms.short: Qualification, right, eligibility to do or be something.
terms.long: Pronounced exactly like 刺客. Used in phrases like 'having no right to…'. On this site, this second meaning is the climax of Act 5.
Another homophone. Fans often link it to the frame of a manga panel, and this site's logo uses a tilted square as a nod to that [FAN ANALYSIS].

terms.short: The sense of sight; visual perception.
terms.long: A homophone that fits a medium as visual as manga. There is no official sign this meaning is intended.

terms.short: Blind spot; an angle that cannot be seen.
terms.long: Literally 'dead angle'. Some fans read it as the emotional blind spot both leads share [FAN ANALYSIS].

terms.short: A phonetic Japanese script, often used for loanwords or emphasis.
terms.long: The official title is written シカク in katakana, not kanji. Because katakana records only sound, the title keeps every meaning of 'shikaku' open.
Yugeru is a kyūketsuki who cannot die. The story uses the vampire not for horror but to talk about the boredom and loneliness of forever.
More casual than 刺客. The official anime site introduces Shikaku as a girl famous as a koroshiya.
Yugeru's condition. The story frames immortality not as a gift but as a dull sentence.

terms.short: A one-shot; a manga story complete in a single issue.
terms.long: Shikaku is a yomikiri. The format forces the author to compress character, conflict, and resolution into one chapter.

terms.short: The Shueisha manga magazine that ran Shikaku in 2014.
terms.long: A companion edition of Jump SQ. Many young manga artists published early one-shots there.
In the 2025 anime adaptation, Shikaku is voiced by Kana Hanazawa and Yugeru by Tomokazu Sugita.
A key beat in Japanese romance. Shikaku takes her kokuhaku to the least private place imaginable: live television.

terms.short: Fan term: a character whose love is obsessive to the point of danger.
terms.long: A community label, not one the story uses. Shikaku is often called one, though she reads better as a child nobody taught how to love [FAN ANALYSIS].
Tatsuki Fujimoto is the mangaka later known for Fire Punch, Chainsaw Man, and Look Back.
